new_statements.translation: [p.50] Note that the data (see appendix) come principally from the varieties spoken in the department of Huánuco, especially Ambo-Pasco, Margos-Yarowilca-Lauricocha (MYL) and Huamalíes. The conclusions of this study apply principally to those varieties [...] [p.52] One can tell that in the second case the particle is bound from the placement of stress ('la fuerza de la voz'), which in Quechua falls on the penultimate syllable: a.'li.cag, NOT 'a.li # cag.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the (phonological) word, so a cliticized/bound element counts toward the penult computation (alicag stressed a.LI.cag).
new_statements.exceptions: None in Toliver. The companion article in the same volume (Weber & Landerman 2008:25-26, general Central Quechua) adds that a word-final long vowel marking 1st person carries stress, and that in Huallaga 'and some other varieties' other word-final long vowels are stressed too; Huamalíes is not named there.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level; used as a diagnostic of word-hood (bound vs free particle). The remark is a pooled generalization over the author's Huánuco data (Ambo-Pasco, MYL, Huamalíes); the illustrating form is written in Ambo-Pasco orthography, so it is not a Huamalíes-specific description. The dedicated description of this variety (Solá 1967, Llata) was not accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement (Toliver 2008:52) is a pooled generalization over the author's Huánuco corpus, which he says comes 'principalmente' from Ambo-Pasco (qva, ambo1252), Margos-Yarowilca-Lauricocha (qvm, marg1254) and Huamalíes (qvh, huam1248); the illustrating word is in Ambo-Pasco orthography. It is therefore evidence for huam1248 only by inclusion, not a Huamalíes-specific description. The dedicated description of this variety is Solá 1967 (based on Llata, capital of Huamalíes = Glottolog dialect huam1249), not accessible. Cancino 2019 describes La Unión (Dos de Mayo) Quechua, which Cerrón-Palomino's 'Alto Marañón' grouping and Domínguez 2006 place with Huamalíes, but it is silent on stress.

new_statements.quote: In the Quechua I dialects stress is maintained in word-final position when the long vowel morpheme referring to first-person subject or possessor is immediately followed by a word boundary, (Length oppositions not connected [...] the first-person morpheme are normally neutralised in word-final position, in which case stress is regularly assigned to the penultimate syllable.) [...] Otherwise, penultimate stress is predominant. More complex, non-penultimate stress patterns, involving word-initial stress and stress dependent on syllable structure, are found in QI Ancash and in QI Cajatambo (cf. Torero 1964: 461; Parker 1976).

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog's penultimate rule and with Toliver 2008 / Weber & Landerman 2008 (existing statement): adds the quantity-insensitive word-final exception for the first-person long vowel and the domain (word boundary, length neutralisation). The statement is at the level of Quechua I / Quechua as a whole; Huamalíes is mentioned only in the dialect survey ('the provinces of Marañón and Huamalíes in the north of the department of Huánuco' in the quantity-insensitive Huánuco area; Solá 1967 = 'concise grammatical description of the Quechua I dialect of Llata in the province of Huamalíes'). The WALS open_url is a bibliographic record with no text; the archive.org copy is lending-res…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level statement, not specific to Huamalíes: in Quechua generally stress is penultimate; in the Quechua I dialects (to which the Huánuco group containing Huamalíes belongs) stress stays on the final syllable when the word ends in the first-person long-vowel morpheme (-: 'I / my'); other word-final length is neutralised, and then stress is regularly penultimate. Word-initial stress and syllable-structure-dependent patterns are reported for quantity-insensitive Ancash and quantity-insensitive Cajatambo only.
new_statements.exceptions: Word-final stress in quantity-insensitive when the word ends in the first-person long vowel; word-final stress after elision of a final syllable (northern Junín, Pacaraos); word-initial and syllable-structure-dependent stress in quantity-insensitive Ancash and quantity-insensitive Cajatambo (not Huánuco).
new_statements.identity_note: Mere Collazos 2018 describes Singa district (Huamalíes province) but the data are Spanish personal-name hypocoristics of bilinguals, not Quechua. Adelaar & Muysken 2004 treat Quechua as a whole and Quechua I as a group; Huamalíes appears only in the dialect survey as part of the Huánuco quantity-insensitive area (Solá 1967 on Llata = Huamalíes), so its stress statements are not lect-specific.
